t: authority_channel.py is the private Rust-supervised connector child: bounded single-line JSONL over anonymous stdio pipes, tracking one in-memory token lease and dispatching approved_effect bodies to the injected handler.
channel_auth.py is the closed bounded framing and one-use broker HMAC layer using only the standard library; rendezvous is private, never an environment variable or log.
serve_connector(handler) runs the connector loop until stdin EOF; __main__ maps its return to a fixed process exit code, with BaseException yielding 2 after cleanup.
receive_ticket(directory) consumes one private bootstrap ticket; connect_broker(ticket) performs one authenticated bounded identity-scoped request over loopback.

stdin line -> length/newline check -> JSON parse -> dict check -> validate_frame(epoch) -> branch token_lease/approved_effect/other; accepted results leave via _write_stdout_frame on stdout using make_frame.
read_frame reads one newline-terminated line with 5s timeout and MAX_LINE bound; write_frame serializes with allow_nan=False, rejects frames over MAX_LINE before writing.
epoch None requires first frame to be connector_start; on success it replies observation ready and enters established state. Later connector_start frames are rejected with exit 2.
Every frame carries exactly six keys with schema cafe.connector.v1, request_id channel, expected_revision 0, nonzero u64 authority_epoch; lines longer than MAX_LINE 16384 are rejected.
Clock strings are canonical decimal u64 with no leading zeros; value 0 is rejected everywhere except the internal parser, and non-ASCII or non-decimal fails.
token_lease body must be exactly {token,expires_unix_ms} with 1-2048 byte token and expiry 0<remaining<=5000ms; make_frame builds the fixed six-key envelope callers must not reshape.

Ticket must be cafe.rendezvous.v1 with host 127.0.0.1, identity broker, port 1-65535, nonzero epoch clock, and 64 lowercase hex secret; POSIX rendezvous dir must be 0700 uid-owned with 0600 broker.sock.
Oversize or unterminated stdin line, bad JSON, non-dict, or validate_frame failure returns process code 2 immediately. Empty read with epoch set returns 0, without epoch returns 1.

Invalid lease body clears active_token/expiry and replies effect_result accepted False and continues; valid lease stores token and replies accepted True. Handler Exception returns 2; BaseException propagates after finally clears lease.
Non-loopback host, challenge mismatch, bad HMAC proof, or unauthenticated response raises broker_rejected; socket errors and timeouts collapse to the same error with no detail.
User sees connector exit code 2 with no stdout frame, or effect_result {accepted:false}: caused by malformed/oversize line, wrong epoch, expired lease, or handler raising Exception.
Blocking stdin readline and stdout writes run via asyncio.to_thread, awaited one at a time; there is a single awaited writer path and no concurrent frame emission.
Line bound is 16384 bytes with limit=MAX_LINE on connections and 5s timeouts on read, write drain, and ticket/connect operations; oversize data fails rather than buffering.
Only standard library (asyncio, hashlib, hmac, json, os, stat, time); service_request/service_result validation delegates to runtime_service_auth; Windows ticket path delegates to windows_auth.
Token material lives only in function-local active_token and is cleared in finally on every exit; module never logs, echoes, or exposes token material on stdout, stderr, or exceptions.
logging_storage.py is the exclusive bounded sanitized trace sink: stdin bytes are data, never a pathname; it creates one fresh stream with no append or file-selection API.
main(argv) parses only --root via a ClosedParser whose error fails closed, then consume(root, sys.stdin.buffer) streams lines into a fresh Sink.
stdin line -> size/newline gate -> trace._json parse -> trace._valid against sink schema -> Sink.write re-validates, JSON-encodes with ensure_ascii/allow_nan=False, appends one \n row.
Sink opens fresh file trace-<32hex>.jsonl, writes rows while open, closes with fsync on success path; closed flag makes close idempotent and _check fail after close.
Before and after every row, fd identity, size==bytes counter, path lstat identity, and root state must match creation values; any mismatch calls _fail and aborts.
Bounds MAX_FILE_BYTES 2097152, MAX_ROWS 4096, MAX_LINE_BYTES 4096 enforced on input and output; empty input (zero rows) is EXIT_INVALID_INPUT, not success.
Exit codes are fixed: 0 success with >=1 row, 3 invalid input line or empty stream, 2 unavailable on OSError/validation infrastructure failure. Only --root is accepted.
Root must be absolute, contain no .., and be named diagnostics; POSIX parent opened via trace._open_root with root state check, diagnostics dir 0700, file 0600 O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW.

Oversize line, missing newline, input_bytes overflow, row cap reached, or trace._valid false returns EXIT_INVALID_INPUT. OSError/ValueError/TypeError/RecursionError/OverflowError returns EXIT_UNAVAILABLE.
_fail raises SinkError diagnostic_sink_unavailable; Sink.__init__ closes descriptors on any BaseException then re-raises, and consume finally closes sink suppressing OSError/ValueError.
Operator sees exit 3 and no trace file rows when a pasted line exceeds 4096 bytes, lacks trailing newline, or has unknown keys; exit 2 means disk/permission or anchor failure, not bad data.
Single-threaded partial-write loop retries os.write until the validated row is fully written; bytes counter advances only by actual count, and count<=0 fails closed.
Success path fsyncs fd before close; parent/root fds and Windows handles released in finally; __init__ failure closes with sync=False to avoid fsync of partial state.
Depends on cafe.runtime_logging helpers _schema, _root_state, _open_root, _safe, _identity, _valid, _json; Windows path uses ctypes kernel32 plus msvcrt with no-delete-sharing handles.
Windows pins every ancestor from volume root with SHARE_READ-only handles and verifies reparse/directory bits; POSIX uses dir_fd-anchored openat plus fstat identity to block symlink and rename swaps.
mcp_chat_digest.py computes deterministic read-only statistics over an already-loaded chat snapshot in one pass, without I/O or control calls; caller owns trust in the supplied events iterable.
execute(name,arguments,events,scan) runs chat_statistics or chat_activity; tool_definitions returns fresh closed schemas for exactly those two tools.

arguments -> _arguments query/start/end/count -> _aggregate single pass (fingerprint+counts+words) -> chat_activity slices buckets by cursor -> _fits_response gate -> ReadResult or response_too_large.

Result selection is closed: invalid_arguments, provider_unavailable, stale_cursor, scan_limited (complete false), response_too_large, or available with error None/complete flag; provider/iterator failures never leak text.
Scan must have exactly five keys with scan_limited bool and bounded ints; any scan damage makes aggregate incomplete, and scan mutation during iteration raises provider_unavailable.
Snapshot identity is content-addressed over ordered events plus unchanged scan; cursors are opaque sha256 commitments to query+fingerprint+offset, never readable chat/login/clock text.
Requires channel 3-25 [a-z0-9_], from<to UTC instants, bucket 1-3600, top 1-50, limit 1-200, bucket count<=1000, cursor<=512 UTF-8 bytes, serialized query<=MAX_REQUEST.
Events validated as cafe.chat_event.v1 with fixed key sets, clock strings, bounded text/badges; words use Unicode casefold split on non-letter/decimal, drop empties and >64 char tokens, no stemming.

Bad arguments return error invalid_arguments; bad scan or aggregate exception returns provider_unavailable; unknown cursor returns stale_cursor; oversize frame returns response_too_large with scan echo when valid.
Rejects str/bytes/dict/IOBase events and the DataReader lazy generator by code-object check; per-event raw line over MAX_EVENT_LINE or cumulative bytes over MAX_SCAN_BYTES raises ValueError.
User sees data None with error scan_limited when chat files were truncated or corrupt, or stale_cursor when paging with an old cursor after the query or snapshot changed.
Single-pass in-memory iteration only; docstring forbids I/O when advancing the iterable, and scan is snapshotted to bytes before the loop to detect concurrent mutation.
Buckets capped at 1000; response bounded by MAX_RESPONSE including duplicated MCP text plus 4301 reserved bytes for numeric IDs; caller still applies final JSON-RPC frame cap.
Imports bounds MAX_EVENT_LINE, MAX_FILES, MAX_REQUEST, MAX_RESPONSE, MAX_SCAN_BYTES and DataReader.events code object from .mcp_server; DataReader supplies plain dicts without provenance markers.
Iterator, validation, and encoding failures return fixed codes without their text; top_emotes is always None with emotes_status metadata_unavailable rather than partial data.

mcp_control.py is the local MCP authority-control plane over select_capsule, start_recording, stop_recording, send_to_obs with the frozen cafe.control_intent.v1 wire contract; without trusted snapshot, approval, and rendezvous every attempt ends blocked.
ControlPlane.execute(tool,args,now_ns) returns a closed MCP envelope under a lock; main CLI builds a plane with no providers so it always replies blocked and exits nonzero.
args -> id checks -> snapshot -> approval load -> wire check -> expiry/reuse -> ticket epoch match -> admission audit pending -> broker HMAC roundtrip -> consume ids -> outcome audit -> reply.

Reply states pending/committed/rejected/interrupted/blocked plus selected for select; success is committed/pending/selected. Uncertain dispatches join uncertain_requests and disable nothing except failed outcome audit sets audit_failed.

Wire must be exact six-key cafe.control_intent.v1 with bound op, token, capsule_id, epoch, revision; folder-bearing bodies, bare wires, mismatched op/capsule/epoch, unknown revision, or token substring in ids are rejected.

Authority reply must be five-key ControlReply with known state, u64 revision, authority-only error code, and receipt rules: committed needs receipt+no error, pending needs neither, others need string error and no receipt.

Module emits only the fixed CONTROL_ERRORS set with no exception text; authority errors accepted only from AUTHORITY_ERRORS. Malformed caller ids answer invalid, never reflected; unknown revisions are None.

Approval must be None, (wire,issued_ns), or {wire,issued_ns} from the injected provider; bare wires rejected. TTL is 30s, future-dated and reused token fingerprints rejected; request ids and tokens have 1024/2048 caps.

Bad request/capsule id, duplicate request_id, unknown capsule, missing providers, no approval, bad wire, expired binding, or ticket epoch mismatch each append an audit line and return rejected or blocked without dialing.

Pre-send transport failure returns blocked control_transport_error; post-send failure consumes ids, marks uncertain, audits interrupted/uncertain_dispatch. Failed outcome audit returns interrupted audit_unavailable and latches audit_failed.
Missing rendezvous dir or fetcher failure raises _NoBridge and maps to blocked mcp_control_unavailable; non-loopback ticket or bad port raises non-ambiguous transport error.

Operator sees blocked confirmation_required when no approval exists yet, blocked mcp_control_unavailable with no providers or bridge, or interrupted uncertain_dispatch after a lost dispatch: inspect status instead of replaying.
All steady state (selected, ticket, seen ids, consumed tokens, uncertain, audit_failed) is in-memory under one threading.Lock held for the whole execute call.
One admission JSONL line with hashed ids is fsynced before dispatch; a dispatch that reaches the broker appends one outcome line. Frames bounded by channel_auth.MAX_LINE with 5s socket timeout.

Stdlib only plus channel_auth framing/MAX_LINE; ticket via channel_auth.receive_ticket cached in memory, secret never logged or in argv, loopback 127.0.0.1 only; ticket_fetcher/connector seams are test-only.

Audit lines carry only fixed keys with sha256 of request/capsule ids; _audit_file anchors every path component (POSIX dir_fd chain, Windows no-delete-sharing handles) and rejects symlinks, non-regular, or nlink!=1 files.
mcp_operator_runbook.py is the static read-only seven-step operator checklist for human-confirmed Cafe workflow; it supplies no direct recorder effect and owns no initialization, framing, or limits.
demo_guide(arguments) returns all steps when step is omitted, one step for integer 1-7, or empty steps with invalid_arguments for any other shape.
read_resource(uri) returns the full guide only for exact cafe://demo/guide, otherwise empty steps with unknown_resource.
Step ids -> _STEPS tuples (instruction, expected, evidence) -> list of dicts with id, depends_on range(1,step), live_status pending, plus control_mode human_confirmed and error field.
Every reply carries live_status pending and control_mode human_confirmed; error is None on success, invalid_arguments on bad input, unknown_resource on bad URI.
Exactly seven fixed steps in order: Discord pop-out, host selector, capsule identity, Confirm recording to MKV, optional OBS send, Twitch JSONL validation, MCP session init.
Exposes exactly one tool demo_guide with optional integer step 1-7, additionalProperties False, readOnly/idempotent true, destructive false, openWorld false.
Exposes exactly one resource cafe://demo/guide named demo_guide with mimeType application/json.
Non-dict arguments, any extra key, missing-or-not-int step, or step outside 1-7 returns full flat shape with empty steps and error invalid_arguments, never a partial guide.
Non-string or non-exact URI returns empty steps with error unknown_resource rather than raising.
Assistant sees empty steps list with error invalid_arguments when it passes a string step or extra keys; consumer must retry with a plain integer 1-7 or no step.
Pure static tuple with no state, locks, or I/O; every call builds fresh reply dicts so callers cannot mutate shared state.
No imports beyond module constants; MCP server owns initialization, notifications, JSON-RPC framing, and response limits.
Window titles and executable names are documented as untrusted data, never identity; AI proposals execute only after the operator clicks Confirm inside Cafe.
mcp_organizer.py is the Windows organizer MCP adapter exposing only observations and proposals; it has no approval provider, token minting, operator wire encoder, subprocess, or path selection.
OrganizerPlane.execute(name,arguments) validates args, calls the trusted provider under a lock, and returns a closed envelope; six tools follow the fixed order status->list->propose->plan_result.
name+args -> validate_arguments rejects extra keys -> provider(name,args) must return {data,error} -> shape check -> plan_id match for plan_result -> 60KB envelope cap.
Validated args wrapped as cafe.organizer.v1 organizer_request with org.<32hex> id, framed with control capability, sent over the HMAC broker handshake; reply checked by request_id.

Six tools: organizer_status, list_discord_windows, propose_recording_plan, plan_result, propose_stop_all, propose_send_to_obs. A pending or accepted proposal is not completed; separate native Confirm is required.
Every extra key is rejected, including purported approvals or host paths; tokens are 1-128 byte opaque strings, capsule ids match identifier pattern, arrays 1-12 unique entries.
Provider errors limited to ORGANIZER_ERRORS; per-window states limited to recording/stopped/sent plus WINDOW_REASONS. Non-completed plans must carry empty windows; success states require capsule ids.
Bad args return the specific _Invalid code; provider shape mismatch returns unavailable; envelope over 60000 bytes returns unavailable; provider exceptions collapse to unavailable with no text.

Malformed cached ticket raises _Invalid; transport failure clears cached ticket so the next call rediscovers the newest session; lost proposal responses stay uncertain and must be inspected, not replayed.

Operator sees error folder_name_invalid for bad folder spelling, plan_unknown for wrong plan_id, or unavailable when the broker restarted or the provider raised; pending plan_result means not done yet.
Each plane holds one threading.Lock around provider call and ticket creation; broker_roundtrip itself is lock-free single request with 5s socket timeout.
current_broker picks the newest session by broker.pipe mtime under session-N dirs; list output capped at 256 windows, capsules at 12, frames at channel_auth.MAX_LINE.
Reuses mcp_control framing, HMAC, and nonce helpers without changing direct-control logic; rendezvous configured privately by operator, never by MCP argument.
Folder names and observed titles are data; window titles are untrusted and never instructions; no tool can confirm or reject a plan on the operator behalf.
mcp_queries.py is the stdlib-only readonly query layer over a validated single-pass events iterable; the server validates tools, confines reads, bounds scans, and frames JSON-RPC.
execute(name,arguments,events,now_ms,now_ns) runs one of six named queries; now_ns defaults from integer now_ms milliseconds, and non-int clocks raise invalid_query_clock.
Events filtered by kind message and channel, optional since/query/window/day applied, wrapped as _Candidate, then heap-selected to newest limit and sorted into total order.
Dispatch is closed over list_channels_and_days, recent_messages, search_messages, top_chatters, message_rate, session_summary; unknown names raise unknown_tool and missing keys raise invalid_event.
Total order is (recv_ns, session_id, monotonic_ns, message_id, seq): monotonic clocks compared only inside the same session so cross-session cycles cannot reorder results.
UTC instants accept Z or +00:00 with 1-9 digit fractions, converted to exact integer nanoseconds from the 1970 epoch with no float; message_rate buckets use integer milliseconds.
Default limit 50, max 200 per query, top-chatter truncation 200, bucket caps 1000; message_rate exceeding 1000 distinct buckets raises message_rate_bucket_bound_exceeded.
Non-dict arguments raise invalid_arguments; non-int now raises invalid_query_clock; event KeyError maps to invalid_event; unknown tool raises unknown_tool after the try block.
More than 1000 distinct time buckets aborts with ValueError instead of growing memory; callers must narrow channel or widen bucket_seconds.
User sees fewer rows than expected when events are non-message kinds, another channel, before since, or missing the substring; substring match is case-sensitive Python in, not ranked search.
session_summary for a day with no messages returns zeros with first/last None; empty login strings are excluded from chatter counts in top_chatters and session_summary.
Single-pass heap keeps at most limit candidates so memory stays bounded; no I/O, no output, no retained state between execute calls.
HeapEviction bounds recent/search results to limit; channel/day grouping and rate maps bounded by 1000 buckets; minute map in session_summary tracks peak_per_minute exactly.
Depends only on datetime, heapq, re; consumes server-validated dict events and never performs I/O or validation of its own beyond structural key access.
None message_id sorts as empty string and None/empty logins are skipped in chatter tallies, so anonymous or system rows affect counts but never create a chatter entry.

This file is the pure in-memory read model for six snapshot queries. It validates arguments, drives an injected provider, projects closed rows, pages with opaque cursors, and never opens files, logs, or network.

tool_definitions returns six fresh detached JSON-schema tool definitions for list_capsules, list_candidate_windows, recording_status, obs_status, messages_by_user, messages_between. Future MCP composition adds them to existing chat tools.

ReadModel.execute(name, arguments, events, scan) is the single query entry. It validates args, resolves prior cursor, calls provider, checks envelope, projects rows, mints next cursor, bounds size, and maps all failures to ReadResult error codes.

Provider contract: provider(kind, arguments) returns None or dict with session_id, authority_epoch, snapshot_id, data, page offset/next_offset/complete. Native list calls also receive offset; status/chat envelopes require offset 0 and next_offset None.

Snapshot envelope must be exactly session_id, authority_epoch, snapshot_id, data, page with offset, next_offset, complete. IDs match _IDENT, epoch is canonical clock; next_offset implies not complete and, if present, is >=1.

Native projections preserve field names: capsules keyed dict to row list with slot alias; windows WindowView list to token/rect subset; recordings list with optional capsule filter; obs_available/services.obs to available/configured/state.

snapshot_id must change on any observation, page-set, or completeness change even if authority revision is unchanged. One ReadModel belongs to one consumer session; session or epoch change clears slots, cursors, observed pages and rejects the call.

Native pages must honor requested offset and limit; next_offset advances by exactly returned row count. Terminal partial page has next_offset None and complete False; complete True is adapter attestation, never inferred from window size or native total.

Pagination state is in-memory OrderedDict cursors keyed by read-prefixed SHA256 reference binding serial, query hash, identity, position, digest, seen set. Remember moves to end and evicts oldest beyond 128 cursors or page fingerprints.

Chat pages hold newest remaining messages, ascending within page; following a cursor moves toward older rows via boundary key. Cursor holds position of first excluded older candidate; more rows than limit triggers next cursor, else terminal.

Flow: canonicalize name/args, hash query, load prior cursor, inject snapshot_id/offset, call provider, validate envelope/session, project rows or chat heap, assign slots, mint cursor, bound response, commit slots/cursors/observed pages only if not response_too_large.

Chat flow filters validated events by kind message, channel, [from,to), user_login, orders by recv_ns/mono/session/msg/seq heap, copies selected dicts at observation time, folds digest over event bytes plus scan and native complete, checks fingerprint.

Bad tool name gives query_unavailable; non-dict args, unknown/extra fields, missing channel/from/to/user_login, bad capsule_id, channel/login/utc shape or from>=to, or limit/cursor shape gives invalid_arguments with unavailable result.

Missing or non-callable provider or provider raise/None gives provider_unavailable. Raw data None gives query_unavailable. Envelope, projection, scan, or generic exception gives invalid_snapshot without leaking exception text.

Unknown cursor or query-hash mismatch gives invalid_arguments; identity change on continuation gives stale_cursor; repeated observation digest change invalidates snapshot and gives stale_cursor or invalid_snapshot. Seen-set regrowth or slot overflow gives query_unavailable.

Oversize JSON representation returns response_too_large with scan preserved and does not commit state. Any scan with scan_limited, corrupt_lines, or truncated_lines surfaces scan_limited error while still returning data.

User sees an available/unavailable envelope with schema cafe.mcp_read.v1, page next_cursor/complete, scan counters, and error text. Failure shows data None, complete False, and one code: invalid_arguments, provider_unavailable, invalid_snapshot, stale_cursor, query_unavailable, scan_limited, response_too_large.

Local memory budgets only: at most 128 cursors/page fingerprints and 4096 slot identities retained; each cursor native identity history also stops at 4096. Exhausting identity bookkeeping returns query_unavailable without recycling aliases; caller starts a new session.

No locks, retries, or timers. Instance is single-consumer and not thread-safe by contract; adapter supplies a fresh DataReader-bounded iterable on each continuation and cursors carry no capability and are meaningless outside issuing instance.

Depends on mcp_queries for DEFAULT_LIMIT, MAX_LIMIT, _utc_to_ns, _Candidate, _recv_ns, _mono_ns, _msg_key and on mcp_server for MAX_RESPONSE, MAX_SCAN_BYTES, MAX_EVENT_LINE, MAX_FILES, _canonical_clock, _utc, _valid_event.

Raw runtime stdout snapshot without adapter identity must fail closed. Public cursors are never forwarded as native snapshot_id; cursors are not credentials and never persisted. No slot-to-ID translation API exists; slots are display aliases keyed by capsule ID and generation.

This file is the bounded stdlib-only MCP stdio server over confined read-only chat files. It frames JSON-RPC, validates tools and read arguments, scans chat via DataReader, delegates optional runtime/statistic/guide modules, and enforces response size caps.

Server.handle is the JSON-RPC dispatcher: validates envelope, handles ping/initialize/notifications, tools/list, resources/list/read, tools/call for read, chat, control, diagnostics, and organizer tools, mapping malformed calls to -32600/-32601/-32602.

serve reads newline-delimited requests bounded by MAX_REQUEST/MAX_EVENT_LINE, rejects overlong/non-JSON with Parse error, writes bounded JSON responses, and substitutes Invalid Request if the frame itself exceeds MAX_RESPONSE. main wires --data/--diagnostics/--organizer flags.

tools lists six frozen chat tools plus optional recent_diagnostics/control/organizer sets; _read_definitions exposes nine frozen typed read queries. Optional dependency descriptors are validated but frozen text is kept so modules cannot widen discovery.

Read flow: validate read args, check provider/model availability, run one bounded DataReader scan finalized before aggregation, call read model or statistics module with values only, then _checked_read_result detachment/validation and bounded response.

DataReader.events walks root/twitch/channel/date.jsonl with directory revalidation, symlink refusal, TOCTOU identity checks, O_NOFOLLOW opens, per-line byte/file caps, and yields only events whose channel and date match path and schema.

Checked read result must have schema cafe.mcp_read.v1, availability/data/error coherence, cursor/complete coherence, runtime/chat/statistics projections valid, list lengths within limit, scan override forcing incomplete page and scan_limited when scan is dirty.

Runtime projection checks capsule/window/recording/obs shapes; statistics checks counts, at most 1000 buckets, top_words <=50, emotes fixed to metadata_unavailable; chat recursively requires embedded cafe.chat_event.v1 rows to pass _valid_event.

Read args allow only declared fields, require channel/from/to when present, check cursor bytes, control_id, limits, utc shape, positive duration, and at most 1000 statistic buckets. Legacy chat/control/diagnostics validators enforce parallel regex and integer ranges.

Server states new->initializing->ready driven by initialize then notifications/initialized. Tools/list reflects data/control/diagnostics/organizer presence; read tools appear only when data root exists. Optional runtime/statistic/guide integrations attach independently or stay absent.

Guide resource lifecycle exposes only cafe://demo/guide; unknown URIs return unknown_resource without reflection. Guide steps must be sequential pending rows with depends_on < id; errors clear steps and oversize guide responses map to response_too_large.

Bounds are invariant: 65536 request/response bytes, 131072 event line bytes, 33554432 scan bytes, 4096 files. Readers stop and set scan_limited past caps; every response path re-checks encoded size including newline before writing.

Data root must be absolute, free of .., fully lstat-pinned with dev/ino identity, symlink-free, regular-file or directory as required, with Windows reparse rejection. Any mismatch raises unsafe_data_path before scanning.

Non-dict, wrong jsonrpc/method, bad id, bad initialize shape, or call before ready returns Invalid Request; unknown method returns Method not found; bad tools/call shape or legacy arg mismatch returns Invalid params; oversize write degrades to Invalid Request.

Bad read args give invalid_arguments; missing provider/model/statistics gives provider_unavailable; scan/aggregation exception gives provider_unavailable for runtime reads else query_unavailable; failed post-check gives invalid_snapshot; oversize gives response_too_large.

Bad channel name, symlink, filename, identity change, overlong line, bad JSON, schema/channel/date mismatch increments corrupt_lines or truncated_lines; exceeding MAX_FILES or MAX_SCAN_BYTES sets scan_limited and ends enumeration early.

User sees fixed failure text data_unavailable_or_result_too_large for legacy/control/diagnostic overflow, or a cafe.mcp_read.v1 envelope with data None, empty page, scan stats, and error invalid_arguments, provider_unavailable, query_unavailable, invalid_snapshot, scan_limited, or response_too_large.

Reader holds no open file across calls; each events generator opens one file at a time with O_NOFOLLOW/NONBLOCK, updates bytes_scanned/files_scanned/corrupt/truncated counters in stats, and is always closed in a finally block before aggregation.

Query instant is frozen once via time.time_ns or validated decimal clock before scanning. No locks or retries; control approval lifetime belongs to control-plane monotonic clock and control result shape is strictly checked before framing.

Optional mcp_runtime_queries, mcp_chat_digest, mcp_operator_runbook, mcp_organizer, runtime_logging, windows_auth are imported lazily and validated; absence or unusable integration never disables old chat queries and cannot leak arbitrary fields.

Protocol version is frozen 2025-11-25 with serverInfo cafe 0.1.0 and capabilities tools listChanged false, resources subscribe false listChanged false. Data, diagnostics, and organizer roots come only from startup flags, never MCP arguments.

Duplicate JSON keys, non-JSON numbers, and dependency-owned mutable state are rejected or detached via re-serialization. Exception text, file paths, passwords, and unknown URIs are never reflected; _meta params are stripped before validation.

This file is closed OBS authentication and admission: endpoint checks, password handling, Hello/Identify math, message decoding, capsule/crop validation, and fixed error codes. Secrets never enter diagnostics and provider errors are never exposed verbatim.
validate_endpoint admits only host exactly 127.0.0.1 and integer port 1-65535; anything else raises loopback_only or invalid_endpoint before any socket, task, or file operation.

open_local_connection validates endpoint, requires websockets 17.2 else dependency_unavailable, opens loopback websocket with fixed timeouts and limits, and maps any failure outside the except suite to connection_failed without context.
decode_message accepts only str within 65536 UTF-8 bytes, rejects duplicate keys and non-JSON numbers, and requires exactly op int plus d dict, else malformed_response.

Hello must be op 0 with rpcVersion 1, obsWebSocketVersion starting 5., optional obsStudioVersion str, and optional salt/challenge pair of 1-1024 valid base64 strings. Returns rpcVersion 1 with no subscriptions plus salted SHA256/based response when challenged.

Identified must carry negotiatedRpcVersion 1 else unsupported_rpc. Each RequestResponse must be op 7 with matching requestType/requestId, bool result, code 100, dict responseData; false result maps to request_failed, other shape to malformed_response.

Capsule validation requires capsule_id matching [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}, feeds non-empty subset of game/camera, descriptors 1-4096 UTF-8 bytes without CR/LF/NUL, exactly three colon parts all non-empty, and distinct descriptors else ambiguous_window.

Crop plan validates four reviewed fields, reads OBS-owned sourceWidth/sourceHeight, rejects overflow beyond source or 100000 bound, emits cropLeft/Top/Right/Bottom; verify requires identical source size and transform values else request_failed.

Auth states: Hello op0 -> Identify op1 with computed authentication if challenged -> Identified op2. Missing password when challenged gives authentication_failed; wrong rpcVersion gives unsupported_rpc at either step.
Non-string password or UTF-8 length over 2048 gives invalid_password and returns presence flag only; no API persists the password and connection logs are disabled via private NullHandler logger.

Crop validation delegates to runtime_service_auth and maps any ValueError to invalid_capsule, so feed/crop key mismatch, non-integers, zero size, or 32-bit overflow surfaces as one fixed capsule code.

All errors are ObsError with only fixed codes loopback_only, invalid_endpoint, invalid_password, authentication_failed, unsupported_rpc, malformed_response, connection_failed, connection_lost, request_failed, invalid_capsule, ambiguous_window, source_conflict, dependency_unavailable, not_connected, operation_uncertain.
User sees only a short fixed code such as authentication_failed, connection_failed, invalid_capsule, or source_conflict. No password, close reason, endpoint detail, or provider string is surfaced.

Single 65536-byte wire limit applies to decoded messages and websocket max_size/max_queue/write buffers. Observed integers accept exact ints or integral finite floats within 0-4294967295, else malformed_response.
Depends on websockets.asyncio.client connect pinned to 17.2 and on runtime_service_auth.validate_crops for crop shape; redirect handling explicitly returns an error to reject untrusted Location URIs.

Logger cafe.obs.private is level above CRITICAL with NullHandler and no propagation so no ancestor handler can observe frames or close reasons. Password is consumed only by Identify construction and deleted by caller after use.

This file is the OBS WebSocket v5 semantic client and I/O orchestration glue. It opens a loopback session, runs Hello/Identify/Identified, then drives correlated scene and input requests sequentially with no credential storage.

connect opens a local connection, waits 5s for Hello, decodes and builds Identify payload, sends it, waits for Identified, validates it, and returns an ObsBridge. Any hello/handshake transport failure maps to authentication_failed after quiet close.

send_capsule validates capsule and crops, locks, builds scene-qualified input names Scene.capsule.role sorted by role, ensures scene, checks kinds, lists items, ensures each source, applies crop, and returns scene/outcome/feeds with input_name and scene_item_id.

_exchange increments sequence to cafe-N requestId, sends op 6 Request with type/data, awaits reply within 5s, decodes and validates correlation via obs_auth, returning responseData. Transport failure marks broken, closes, and raises operation_uncertain.
Ensures scene named Café exists: GetSceneList must return list of dicts with sceneName str; creates it if absent, else malformed_response. No other scene name is used.

GetInputList must return unique inputName/inputKind strings; GetSceneItemList must return unique sourceName to int sceneItemId. Duplicates or bad shapes raise malformed_response; duplicate scene sources raise ambiguous_window.

Existing inputs must already be window_capture with window equal to descriptor else source_conflict. Missing input creates window_capture with fixed method/priority/cursor/client_area/compatibility/audio flags disabled; missing scene item creates disabled item, then verifies, crops, enables, and confirms enabled True.

Crop apply disables item, confirms disabled False, reads transform, plans via OBS-owned dimensions, sets transform, re-reads, and verifies. Any enabled-state or dimension mismatch raises request_failed.

Session states: handshake-completed open, closed, broken. Lock serializes one capsule exchange at a time; send after closed/broken or null socket gives not_connected; first transport failure latches broken and closes.
Bad Hello decode, Identify build, or Identified validation closes quietly and propagates the obs_auth code. Password local is deleted after payload construction regardless of outcome.

Send/receive timeout or provider exception sets _broken, closes socket, raises operation_uncertain without surfacing provider strings. Decode or correlation errors propagate malformed_response, request_failed, or related fixed codes.

Operator sees fixed codes such as not_connected, source_conflict when an input already exists with a different kind or window, ambiguous_window on duplicate scene sources, request_failed when enable or crop verification disagrees, or operation_uncertain after a mid-exchange disconnect.

All mutating exchanges hold one asyncio.Lock so capsule setup, kind checks, item creation, crop, and enable steps run sequentially per bridge. Close is idempotent; context manager closes on exit and never suppresses exceptions.

Every network wait is bounded at 5.0 seconds for hello, send, receive, and close. Quiet close awaits close within bound, re-raises cancellation, and swallows other errors so handshake failures never hang.

All validation, endpoint admission, authentication math, and error closure belong to cafe.obs_auth; this module implements no copies, stores no credentials, and imports only obs_auth plus asyncio and json.
Window rectangles are never substituted for OBS-owned source dimensions; only the four reviewed crop fields are sent. Secrets are deleted after Identify and never retained on the bridge or in logs.

runtime_logging reads only the host-bound closed sanitized runtime trace stream: it pins the diagnostics root, selects the newest trace file, validates rows against a hashed schema, and returns the bounded tail.

runtime_service_auth is the closed private-pipe validator for service requests and results. It accepts only status/close/configure_obs/start_chat/send_capsule shapes and bounded nonsecret results, with fixed codes and no rejected values.

recent(root, limit) never accepts a path from MCP arguments; root comes from server startup. It loads schema, pins root identity, scans at most 64 names, picks max mtime/name file, reads it, and returns rows tail plus incomplete_tail/truncated flags.

validate_service_request rejects before any handler, network, task, or file runs; validate_service_result allows only accepted/closed booleans, obs/chat enums, fixed codes, and canonical u64 counters as strings across the authority boundary.

Schema file src/contracts/runtime_logging.json is read through pinned descriptors with 65536 cap and must hash to 7aba1cda71ed585c4313e0577717a14bd42b09bc1e122315d0f4f846e2e301b9, else diagnostics_unavailable.

Each row must match schema fields exactly, sequential seq from 1, elapsed_ms 0-86400000, enum membership for event/op/bridge/reason/result_state/result_code/stage/recording_state, bounded counters, optional 40-hex commit and 64-hex authority hash.

Crops require feeds non-empty subset of game/camera, crops keys exactly feed keys, each crop x/y/width/height uint32, non-zero size, and x+width/y+height within 4294967295, else service_request_rejected.

Accepted bodies: status/close with op only; configure_obs with port 1-65535 and password absent or provided value 1-1024 UTF-8 bytes; start_chat with channel [a-z0-9_]{1,25}; send_capsule with capsule id, distinct 3-part descriptors, and valid crops.

Trace bounds: 2097152 file bytes, 4096 rows, 4096 line bytes, 64 directory entries. Oversize size, row count, line length, or entry count fails closed; only an unterminated append tail is excluded, never a malformed complete row.

Root and schema paths must be absolute without .., fully lstat-pinned by dev/ino, symlink- and reparse-free, regular or directory as required, single link for files, with POSIX ancestor descriptors and rechecks before, during, and after reads.

Flow: validate limit 1-32, load schema, pin root, open descriptor, scandir with strict name trace-[0-9a-f]{32}.jsonl, stat each, pick newest, verify root state, read bytes, split lines, parse each with duplicate-key rejection, validate sequence, slice last limit rows.

Any OSError, ValueError, TypeError, RecursionError, OverflowError, identity change, size breach, schema mismatch, empty table, or missing candidates raises TraceError diagnostics_unavailable with no filesystem or record detail.

Request mismatch raises service_request_rejected; result enum, code, or counter mismatch raises service_result_rejected. Codes carry only closed, not_configured, already_running, operation_uncertain, unavailable with no values.

Operator sees diagnostics_unavailable with no path or row detail when trace root, schema hash, file size, row shape, or append state is wrong, or a truncated tail flag when rows exceed limit or file ends mid-line.

Caller sees service_request_rejected for bad op, port, password shape, channel, capsule, descriptor, or crop, and service_result_rejected for bad state crossing back; Rust parent must validate the same body before writing its pipe.

Files open with O_RDONLY/O_NOFOLLOW/O_NONBLOCK, identity and size rechecked against pre-stat and post-stat plus root state, read capped at maximum+1, descriptors always closed; schema read capped at 65536.

Depends only on stdlib hashlib, json, os, pathlib, re, stat and the contract file at src/contracts/runtime_logging.json. No endpoint, executable, path, or arbitrary OBS request is accepted by either module.

Path confusion is contained: logging root and schema never come from MCP input, pipe bodies never carry endpoints or filesystem paths, NUL bytes fail text checks, and error codes never include rejected values or secrets.

This file is the Rust-owned private service sidecar. It admits only the parent-supplied private chat directory, speaks the closed stdin/stdout frame protocol, dispatches validated service ops to RuntimeServices, and never exposes chat, passwords, or exception text.

serve(directory) loops reading bounded stdin frames, emits a ready observation on first epoch, dispatches service_request frames, writes service_result replies, and exits 0 on accepted close else 2. main runs serve for one argv path.

dispatch validates the body then handles configure_obs, start_chat, send_capsule, status/close via RuntimeServices; any handler exception returns projection with accepted False rather than leaking errors.

Private root must be absolute, free of .., strictly resolved identical, symlink- and reparse-free on every ancestor, a directory, and on POSIX owned by caller with no group/other permission bits; Windows checks ACL ownership, other platforms rejected.

Private frames must be non-empty, at most MAX_LINE with trailing newline, strict JSON with unique keys and no non-JSON numbers, passing channel_auth.validate_frame for the epoch as initiator, else private_frame_rejected.

Flow: first frame establishes epoch and replies ready; later frames must be service_request, body dispatched, result wrapped by make_frame service_result, revalidated, written via bounded _write; close op returns after reply. Stdout carries only closed protocol.

projection reads RuntimeServices.status, stringifies message counters as canonical u64 strings or None, merges accepted flag, and validates through validate_service_result so only bounded nonsecret state crosses back.

Epoch states: none until first valid frame, then fixed epoch with ready emitted once. Empty stdin ends 0 only after epoch established else 2; non-service_request kind or close result determines 2 vs 0 exit.

Dispatcher pins private root at construction, owns one RuntimeServices, and injects loopback OBS connect and chat producer seams. OBS is always 127.0.0.1; chat always uses its reviewed official endpoint via twitch_chat.run_chat.
Empty, overlong, unterminated, non-UTF8, duplicate-key, bad-number, or epoch-mismatched frames raise private_frame_rejected; oversize replies also raise before writing. No credentials appear in argv.
configure_obs failure closes the newly connected client only when replace_obs did not take ownership, awaiting close up to 8s then cancelling; ownership transfers only after successful replacement.

Parent sees only a service_result with accepted bool plus obs/chat enums and fixed obs_code/chat_code values closed, not_configured, already_running, operation_uncertain, unavailable; failures return accepted False rather than text.

Stdin reads via to_thread with MAX_LINE+1 cap; stdout writes are single bounded frames with flush. Close path awaits client close with timeout and cancels on hang; finally clause always closes services.
Single async loop processes one frame at a time; chat production runs with stop event and progress observer, OBS replacement races guarded by explicit ownership transfer and timed close task.

Depends on channel_auth framing, runtime_service_auth validators, runtime_services RuntimeServices/ServiceError, obs_bridge loopback connect, twitch_chat producer, and on POSIX/Windows ownership checks; no public listener or credential store.

Password local is cleared after connect dispatch and frame bodies are deleted after use. Provider exception context and close reasons never escape; stdout never carries chat content, passwords, logging, or tracebacks.

This file owns mechanical OBS and chat lifetimes. The parent supplies authentication, framing, paths and tests; this module only holds the OBS client, chat task, counters and bounded shutdown. It cannot choose endpoints or paths.
ServiceError carries only one of 5 domain codes: closed, not_configured, already_running, operation_uncertain, unavailable. Unknown codes are coerced to unavailable. Callers match on args[0].
_code extracts a valid code from an exception args[0], else returns unavailable. It centralizes mapping so old OBS errors and chat failures surface as the same closed code set.
Public surface is replace_obs, publish_capsule, start_chat, observe_chat, status and close. All mutating async calls take an asyncio lock; observe_chat and status and _chat_done are synchronous.

replace_obs requires an object with callable send_capsule and close, else raises unavailable without taking the lock. It closes the old client first; old-close failure stores obs_code and raises that code.

If close is requested while replace_obs awaits old.close, the new client is never installed or leaked. It is closed in a bounded task with timeout 8.0 s; timeout, cancel or error raises unavailable, else closed is raised.

publish_capsule raises closed when closed, not_configured when no OBS client, or the mapped OBS error code on send failure. If close lands after a successful send it raises operation_uncertain because delivery is ambiguous.

publish_capsule forwards capsule_id and feeds, plus crops only when not None, to obs.send_capsule and returns its result. On success obs_code is cleared to None; on failure obs_code stores the mapped code.

start_chat takes a parent producer_factory(stop_event). It rejects a closed owner, a still-running chat with already_running, factory exceptions and non-fresh coroutines with unavailable. Only a newly created coroutine object is accepted.
A Task or Future from elsewhere is never adopted or cancelled here because it could belong to someone else. Freshness is enforced via iscoroutine plus CORO_CREATED state before wrapping in a task.

Chat progress flows in through observe_chat dict with u64 counters plus bool connected, is stored when a chat task exists and is not done, is refreshed from task result in _chat_done, and flows out through status.

observe_chat validates exact keys messages, malformed, reconnects, connections plus connected, bool connected, and each counter int in 0..18446744073709551615. Invalid input raises unavailable. Stale updates after close or task end are silently ignored.

Chat states are idle, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled. _chat_done sets connected False, maps cancelled to unavailable, exception to its mapped code, success to None, and copies only valid u64 result counters else None.

OBS states are absent, configured, closed, failed with parallel obs_code. status refreshes a finished chat before returning closed, obs, obs_code, chat, chat_code, chat_connected and counters. Shutdown sets closed or failed.

A user would see publish rejected as not_configured before OBS is set, closed after close, already_running on double chat start, or operation_uncertain when publish wins the race with close. No log or stdout text is produced here.

_shutdown takes no operation lock so an unresponsive publish cannot block closing its transport. close sets closed once, spawns one shutdown task, waits without waiting for cancellation acknowledgement, and re-raises caller cancellation while shutdown continues.

Shutdown waits at most 8.0 s for chat plus OBS close, then cancels stragglers. _consume drains completed-task exceptions to avoid warnings. Any pending or failed OBS close marks obs failed and raises unavailable for the Rust owner to reap.

_chat_done ignores callbacks from a superseded task by identity check against self._chat. status calls _chat_done again when done, so repeated status calls after completion are idempotent and cannot double-count.

This file runs an anonymous read-only Twitch IRC client over verified TLS, logs in as justinfan, answers PING, and persists parsed chat events through the durable JsonlWriter. All outbound frames pass through readonly_send; nothing is written to stdout, stderr or logs.

Entries are run_chat(channel, root, url, max_connections, stop_event, backoff, sleep, session_id, progress) returning closed counters, and parse_irc(line) returning tags/prefix/command/params or None. run_chat validates channel, url and options first.

Defaults are OFFICIAL_URL wss://irc-ws.chat.twitch.tv:443, receive timeout 0.5 s, buffer limit 1048576 bytes, poll 0.05 s. Only the official URL or explicit ws://127.0.0.1:port fixture URLs are accepted.

Socket text accumulates in buf, splits on newline, each line goes through parse_irc/_parse_irc, then _handle_line. Outcomes are appended, reconnect, or ignored; malformed lines increment malformed and never raise.

_parse_irc strips one CR/LF, left spaces, rejects control chars, parses optional @tags with unescaping and duplicate-key rejection, optional prefix, command and colon-trailing params. Any shape violation returns None.

_unescape_tag decodes backslash escapes with table colon->semicolon, s->space, backslash, r, n; unknown escapes drop the backslash and trailing lone backslash is dropped. It operates per tag value only.

_build_event maps PRIVMSG to message, NOTICE to notice, JOIN/ROOMSTATE to join_state, CLEARCHAT/CLEARMSG to clear, RECONNECT to reconnect, else ignore. Channel commands with wrong channel are ignored; bad shapes raise _Malformed.

Event validation bounds are text max 16384 chars, message_id 1..128, display-name max 128, badges max 64 entries with name/version 1..64 and no slash in version, tmi-sent-ts u64 only, login lowercased and matched.

PING with missing or empty trailing param counts malformed 1 without replying. PING send failure counts malformed 1. RECONNECT builds an event and appends it; build or writer invalid_event maps to reconnect plus malformed 1.

For normal lines _Malformed maps to ignored plus malformed 1. Writer invalid_event maps the same. Other ChatError propagates and tears down the connection. Appended events return appended and increment messages.

run_chat owns JsonlWriter(root,channel) and counters messages, malformed, reconnects, connections. progress callback receives that dict plus connected bool. Progress exceptions are converted to ChatError storage_failed.

Per connection: open, send NICK plus CAP REQ plus JOIN, observe False, read loop with flush_due and observe per batch, break on stop, RECONNECT frame, or error, then observe False and close. connections increments per attempt, reconnects increments after the first.

Backoff delay is current_backoff plus uniform jitter up to 100 percent, capped at backoff_max, doubling per failure. _backoff_sleep polls stop_event every 0.05 s with shielded sleep so stop aborts early and cancels the waiter.

Receive uses wait_for 0.5 s; timeout only flushes due writes. Bytes are UTF-8 decoded else malformed. Non-str messages count malformed. buf over 1048576 bytes counts malformed and resets. Trailing partial line at connection end counts malformed 1.

A tester would see no chat file growth during outages, gaps in per-day JSONL, rising malformed or reconnects counters, and eventual return of closed counters. Raised errors carry only domain codes like network_failed or storage_failed, with no printed logs.

Channel matching is case-insensitive against # plus lowercased channel. _U64_RE and max 2^64-1 gate sent_at clocks. Login candidates are login tag then prefix nick, lowercased, matched against 1..25 alphanumerics plus underscore.

Depends on twitch_storage for ChatError, JsonlWriter, open_connection, readonly_send and validators. Writer is always closed in finally. Nick is justinfan plus 0..9999999999 random suffix per process run.

This file provides the closed Twitch endpoint, read-only IRC sends, and confined durable JSONL storage under root/twitch/channel per-day files. It enforces allowlists, symlink and ACL confinement, fsync durability, and never repairs torn tails on read.

ChatError carries only 8 codes: invalid_channel, invalid_endpoint, network_failed, readonly_command, invalid_event, unsafe_path, storage_failed, transport_unavailable. Unknown codes coerce to storage_failed.

validate_channel requires str, lowercases it, and accepts only 3..25 chars of a-z0-9_. Anything else raises invalid_channel. The lowercased value is the canonical channel used for paths and event checks.
validate_url accepts exactly the official wss URL or ws://127.0.0.1 with port 1..65535, empty or slash path, no userinfo, query or fragment, with exact string form. All else raises invalid_endpoint.

validate_options requires max_connections None or int >=1, backoffs finite in 0..60, callable sleep, and session identity 1..96 chars. Missing session_id is generated as chat- plus 12 random hex bytes. Backoff initial is clamped to max.

open_connection validates URL and requires websockets version 17.2, uses a silenced private logger, no proxy, no compression, open timeout 5 s, close 1 s, no ping, max 131072 byte frames and queue 4. Failures map to network_failed.

readonly_send rejects commands containing CR or LF and allows only NICK justinfan plus digits, the exact CAP REQ tags+commands string, JOIN #channel, or PONG with 1..512 safe chars. All else raises readonly_command before any send.

validate_event requires exact 11 fields, schema cafe.chat_event.v1, canonical channel, received_at with u64 monotonic_ns and UTC ISO timestamp, optional u64 sent_at, bounded ids, text max 16384, closed kind set, valid session identity, and badges shape.

append validates the event, rejects poisoned or closed writers and channel mismatch, serializes canonical compact JSON plus newline, rejects lines over 131072 bytes, writes per-day files, and fsyncs every 20 events or 2.0 s via flush_due.

Any OSError, Unicode or value error during append poisons the writer, closes its descriptor, and raises storage_failed. A poisoned writer rejects all later appends and its close also raises storage_failed.

Writer states track fd, current day, pending count, last sync, closed and poisoned flags plus events and syncs counters. Day rollover closes the file; close syncs and marks closed. Poisoned implies closed.

Every root, twitch dir, channel dir and file is checked for symlinks, regular/dir type, positive inode, and on Windows reparse points. Files open with O_NOFOLLOW, fstat identity is compared before and after, and roots are resolved strictly with double lstat checks.
If a non-empty day file does not end in newline, append closes and raises storage_failed without writing. Paths with .. components or failed canonicalization raise unsafe_path.

read_jsonl_file opens read-only with O_NOFOLLOW, yields only complete valid records, counts overlong skips as invalid, counts a final torn line as truncated and stops without yielding it, and counts bad JSON or failed validation as invalid.

A tester would see chat capture stop with storage_failed on unsafe paths or torn files, per-day .jsonl gaps, and CLI exit 2 on domain errors or 130 on interrupt. No event payloads are printed; errors carry only codes.

main parses --channel and --data, validates them, resolves data to absolute, requires the directory, then runs run_chat against only OFFICIAL_URL. Relative-import failure falls back to cafe.twitch_chat; ChatError maps to exit 2.
Line cap is 131072 bytes; sync policy defaults are 20 events and 2.0 s with bounds 1..1000 and 0..10. File mode is 0600. Side effects are flushed file data plus parent directory sync.

windows_auth receives an owner-only broker ticket over a Windows named pipe using stdlib ctypes. No secret lives in rendezvous metadata; ACL, owner, reparse and server-identity failures reject admission with no alternate transport.

cafe_mcp is the Windows MCP launcher. It reads APPDATA, prepends the connector directory to sys.path, and delegates to cafe.mcp_server main with organizer-root APPDATA/cafe-shell/authority. Missing APPDATA exits 2.

Flow is _api binds kernel32/advapi32 signatures, _owner captures the current process SID, _check_acl gates the directory and broker.pipe file, then _receive_ticket validates metadata, opens the pipe, checks the server PID, and reads one ticket line.
_api binds 9 kernel functions for process, pipe and file IO plus 7 security functions for token, SID and ACL inspection, with explicit argtypes and restype. No other system APIs are used.

_owner opens the current process token with 0x0008 query access, requires token size in 1..65536 bytes, and returns both the buffer and the embedded SID pointer. Failures raise rendezvous_owner_failed.

_check_acl rejects reparse points, requires dir versus regular-file mode match, requires GetNamedSecurityInfo success, owner SID equality, and for directories the DACL_PROTECTED flag. It requires exactly 1 ACE which must be ACCESS_ALLOWED, non-inheriting, mask 0x001f01ff, owner SID.
Any ACL, owner, reparse or descriptor-control failure raises insecure_rendezvous; security API failures raise rendezvous_acl_failed. Both deny admission before any pipe metadata is read.

Metadata broker.pipe over 1024 bytes raises invalid_rendezvous_metadata. JSON must be exactly schema, pipe_name, authority_pid with schema cafe.rendezvous.endpoint.v1. pipe_name must be cafe-broker- plus 64 lowercase hex (76 chars total). PID must be int in 2..4294967295 and not self.

Pipe address is built as \\pipe\ plus the validated name. WaitNamedPipe waits 5000 ms, CreateFile opens with 0xc0000000 generic read/write, no sharing, and 0x00110000 SQOS identification flags so the server cannot impersonate the client.

After connect the server PID from GetNamedPipeServerProcessId must equal the metadata PID else rendezvous_server_changed. The ticket read has a 5 s deadline, PeekNamedPipe polling every 0.005 s, over-limit data raises ticket_too_large.

Ticket framing requires exactly one newline-terminated JSON value: missing newline, extra bytes, or multiple lines raise invalid_ticket. Empty reads and read failures raise incomplete_ticket; deadline expiry raises rendezvous_timeout; broken ack raises rendezvous_ack_failed.

The pipe handle is always closed via CloseHandle in finally. The ack {received:true} plus newline must be fully written. _receive_ticket never retries; each failure raises a ValueError code to the caller.

A user would see MCP startup refuse to connect: insecure rendezvous, unavailable pipe, server-changed identity, or invalid metadata errors, or immediate exit 2 when APPDATA is missing. No secret is logged or stored in metadata.
windows_auth depends only on ctypes, json, os, pathlib, stat and time plus Windows kernel32/advapi32. cafe_mcp depends only on os, pathlib and sys path setup before importing cafe.mcp_server.

Trust rests on the pre-validated rendezvous directory ACL plus exact pipe-name shape plus live server-PID equality. Without all three, a spoofed pipe or replaced server could deliver a ticket; any mismatch aborts before the ticket is accepted.

This module owns bounded private connector frames and one-use broker HMAC admission. Owner-only Unix sockets or Windows named pipes deliver the one-use secret; request data never constructs an authenticated peer.

Entries are read_frame and write_frame for newline JSON with 5 s deadlines and 16384 byte cap, plus BrokerAuthority start on 127.0.0.1 with nonzero epoch. start_control adds a typed ControlHandler path.

Frames flow as canonical JSON plus newline over async IO. make_frame builds schema cafe.connector.v1 with kind, channel request_id, string epoch, expected_revision 0 and object body. Oversize encode or IO timeout maps to frame_too_large, read/write failures.

Decoding uses UniqueJson to reject duplicate object keys as invalid_json instead of silently keeping the last. Floats that cannot round-trip, truncated reads and timeouts map to invalid_json, incomplete_frame, read_timeout.

Authority frames allow connector_start empty, approved_effect with 1..64 char action, service_request by closed validator, token_lease with 1..2048 char token expiring within 5000 ms. Connector frames allow observation ready bool, effect_result accepted bool, service_result by validator.
lease_frame requires sink private, ttl 1..5000 ms, token 1..2048 chars. It computes expiry with overflow check, builds a token_lease frame, and revalidates it; bad routes raise lease_route_denied.

start binds TCP on 127.0.0.1 ephemeral port, creates a 32 byte secret from entropy, serves one rendezvous ticket over UDS or named pipe, then challenges each TCP peer with broker auth nonce and verifies HMAC-SHA256 proof with constant-time equal.

Non-loopback bind or zero epoch fails loopback_only. Entropy, bind, or address failures abort start. Wrong identity, epoch, proof length or HMAC mismatch silently drops the connection without an authenticated peer. One-shot brokers burn the secret after first success.

AuthenticatedBrokerPeer tracks epoch plus live, connection_live and optional request_live flags with deadline. is_live requires all set flags and deadline not passed; for_actor_request clones the peer once per actor with active flag and deadline.

Control connections use a 1 slot channel: the reader revokes on overflow or invalid frame, callbacks run serially in spawn_blocking with 16384 byte reply cap and CONTROL_REPLY_DEADLINE, and each connection is capped at 15 s.

Invalid epoch, capability or body sends capability_denied and breaks the reader. Dead peer, oversize handler response, handler lock failure, or reply timeout breaks the loop. Reader abort and RevokeConnection clear liveness on drop.

Closed child commands allow status/close empty, configure_obs with port 1..65535 and password absent or provided up to 1024 chars, start_chat with lowercase channel up to 25 chars, and send_capsule with 1..2 game/camera descriptors plus matching crops and nonzero extents.

Service results require exact fields with closed obs/chat enums, nullable bools, nullable codes from the 5 closed set, and nullable u64-string counters. Anything else is rejected as capability violation.

A tester would see bind_failed, rendezvous failures, capability_denied errors, or status showing host 127.0.0.1, port, epoch and effects count. Failed HMAC simply drops the peer with no authenticated session and no secret disclosure.

Entropy reads /dev/urandom on Unix or BCryptGenRandom on Windows; failures raise entropy_unavailable and test faults zeroize first. Drop aborts listener tasks and removes broker.sock and broker.pipe plus the rendezvous directory.

This file is the single-writer append-only authority log of control and media receipts. Records are canonical JSON chained by SHA-256 in length-prefixed frames with a 4 byte CJOK trailer. Staging writes header plus body; only commit appends the trailer and flushes.

Entries are open, stage_control plus commit or append_control, plus append_service_configuration, append_confirmed_intent/result, append_media_intent and publish_media. Reads are records, recovery_status, interrupted_bytes and snapshot.

Each record has exactly 9 fields with genesis prior of 64 zeros. The digest covers the 8 field preimage in canonical sorted-key compact bytes; floats anywhere fail. Bodies over 1048576 bytes are rejected.

Append tokens move Pending to Committed only through commit after trailer flush. Pending carries stage_id and event_id; Committed carries sequence, event_id and digest. Only one staged frame may exist; a second stage raises journal_pending.

open takes a separate .lock sidecar lock or fails journal_locked, then scans from offset zero. Short headers or short bodies quarantine as interrupted suffix; bad length complement, zero length, oversize, bad trailer or failed replay aborts journal_corrupt with no side effects.

A torn suffix is written to a create_new .interrupted sidecar or numbered sibling, parent-synced, then the journal is truncated to the prefix and flushed, reopening as Interrupted with exact suffix bytes preserved. RecoveryStatus is Clean otherwise.

Each record must have canonical bytes equal to stored bytes, matching session, epoch, exact next sequence, fresh event_id, chained prior_digest and digest. Kinds allowed are service_configuration, confirmed_control_intent/result, control, media_intent and media_published.

Confirmed intents require 7 exact fields, valid identifiers, 64 hex identity and args hashes, effect ctl.plus hash, revision exactly sequence minus 1, fresh request, and registry-known capsule for non-folder ops. Results require 3 fields and a matching open intent.

Service configuration stores only service obs or chat plus secret_present bool; chat with secret present is rejected. Event is service-config.plus hash, duplicates by request or payload request_id are rejected as journal_invalid.

Media intent binds a fresh media_id to one safe name. publish_media requires safe staged and published names, non-symlink dir and file, nonzero bytes, fsyncs staged input, renames without clobbering unless same name, then commits byte_len plus sha256 receipt.

stage_control replays committed control records on scratch and rejects non-admitted requests as journal_invalid. commit mismatches stage identity as journal_pending. Any write or flush failure poisons the handle; later calls fail journal_io.

Names must be one normal relative component with no separators, dot segments or NUL. Hex must be exactly 64 lowercase chars. Identifiers must be 1..96 chars starting alphanumeric. Media ids and event ids must be fresh.

Exclusivity is a persistent sidecar file lock held for the handle lifetime; dropping releases it. Staged ids come from a process-wide atomic counter. Durability flushes file data then parent directory; faults for file, parent or directory are injectable in tests.

Every commit fsyncs the file and parent directory; Unix fsyncs the directory fd, Windows requires NTFS policy. Publish uses atomic rename, or no-replace on Windows. Handles are never unlinked; lock ordering releases data before the lock field.

A user would see recording or control operations refuse with journal_locked, journal_corrupt, journal_invalid, journal_pending, journal_media or journal_io, or a restart report Interrupted with quarantined bytes. No paths or input excerpts are included in errors.

Control replay delegates to capsule_registry admission; media paths delegate to windows_journal_policy on Windows. Snapshot exposes only the durable control ledger; staged frames are never visible in records.

PairingBook is the trusted Rust-only admission boundary that binds a capsule feed to a resolved window, generation, layout revision and crop, storing one immutable Binding per feed_id for later capture.

PairingBook.pair receives PairRequest with &mut Registry and &WindowRegistry, snapshots authority, validates person, resolves window, checks crop, allocates generation, applies AddFeed envelope, inserts Binding only when reply is Admitted.

Two-phase path: propose validates against a Snapshot and returns single-use PairProposal with envelope plus binding without mutating state; commit_proposed verifies the envelope was durably admitted then inserts the binding.

Control and data flow: PairRequest fields become Binding fields verbatim plus computed feed_generation; the same ids plus generation become Command::AddFeed inside an intent Envelope with schema, epoch and expected revision for Registry.apply.
checked_crop requires layout_revision equal to view layout revision else StaleCrop; width and height nonzero; x+width and y+height within view rect using checked arithmetic else InvalidCrop.

Generation invariant: feed_generation equals highest_generation+1 via checked_add; GenerationExhausted on u64 overflow. Capsule person_label must equal request person_label else WrongPerson; unknown capsule id yields UnknownCapsule.

Uniqueness invariant: bindings must not already contain feed_id and no existing feed in the capsule may use the same Role, else AlreadyPaired. Duplicate feed_id across capsules is rejected by authority as duplicate_feed.
If request authority_epoch or expected_revision differs from snapshot, propose returns AuthorityRejected stale_pair_proposal with no state change and no envelope emitted.

commit_proposed rejects with AuthorityRejected pair_not_committed unless committed epoch matches and revision equals envelope expected_revision+1; then rechecks duplicate feed, capsule existence, feed role and generation, window and crop.

current looks up Binding by feed_id else FeedUnavailable, then revalidates against live Registry snapshot and live window: person, role, generation, window generation and crop must still hold else FeedUnavailable or Window/Stale/Invalid errors.

User sees pairing refused and no recording for that feed: wrong person label, unknown capsule, already-paired role or feed, stale window layout after resize, crop outside window, or stale authority revision requiring retry with fresh snapshot.

Bindings map starts empty via new; entries are only added by pair or commit_proposed and never updated or removed here; bindings() clones all values; current() is a read-only revalidation, not a state transition.
Depends on Registry snapshot/apply for admission and generation watermark, and on WindowRegistry resolve for WindowView; WindowError converts into PairError::Window via From and propagates unchanged.

PairRequest deliberately has no Deserialize; only trusted Rust code constructs it. Accepting deserialized pairing intent would bypass the Main durable-admission boundary enforced by propose and commit_proposed.
pair_by_executable always returns ExecutableOnlyForbidden. No executable-name lookup path exists; callers must pair by explicit capsule, feed, window handle and crop.

Registry is the zero-effect in-memory capsule and feed admission kernel: a deterministic pure state machine that decodes control envelopes and admits CreateCapsule, AddFeed, RemoveFeed and Propose with no I/O, clocks, threads or network.

Entry via Registry::new(epoch) starting at revision 0 and watermark 0; observation only through owned Snapshot clones containing epoch, revision, highest_generation, capsules, proposals and seen request ids.

Wire entry decode_and_apply rejects payloads longer than MAX_ENVELOPE_BYTES with Oversized, deserializes directly into typed Envelope so duplicates and unknown fields fail as Malformed, then runs shared validation and apply.

Data flow: JSON string to Envelope with schema, kind, request_id, clocks and tagged Command body; apply returns Reply with request_id, Admitted or Rejected state, revision, optional error code, and Receipt only on admission.

apply follows exact six-step order: structural validation, admitted-request deduplication, epoch and expected-revision preconditions, read-only command checks, checked revision+1, then atomic commit. Any rejection leaves all fields untouched.

Commit installs capsule, feed, removal or proposal, advances revision by one, records request_id in seen_requests, updates highest_generation for capsule and feed creation, and returns Admitted with Receipt at the new revision.

Clock serializes as decimal string and deserializes only canonical decimal u64 strings: ASCII digits, nonempty, no leading zeros except 0, no signs or JSON numbers, no overflow. All other forms are Malformed.

Validation order is fixed: schema must equal cafe.control.v1, kind must be intent, request_id and capsule, feed and proposal ids must be 1-128 ASCII alnum/dash/underscore, labels nonblank up to 256 bytes, descriptions nonblank up to 512 bytes.

Per-command preconditions checked in exact order: duplicate_capsule and generation_reused; capsule_not_found, duplicate_feed, duplicate_role, generation_reused; feed_not_found and generation_mismatch; proposal_exists, capsule/feed existence and generation_mismatch.

Generation contract: new capsule or feed generation must be strictly greater than highest_generation watermark, which then becomes that generation. Role slot is Game or Camera snake_case; one feed per role per capsule.

Failure codes returned in Reply.error at unchanged revision: invalid_schema, invalid_kind, invalid_identity, invalid_payload, duplicate_request_id, stale_epoch, stale_revision, plus per-command codes and revision_overflow on u64 wrap.
Wire failures surface as oversized_envelope, malformed_envelope, invalid_schema, invalid_kind, invalid_identity, invalid_payload via Display; DecodeError carries no input excerpts or host paths.

User sees an operation refused with a short code such as stale_revision, duplicate_request_id, duplicate_role or generation_mismatch; state is unchanged and caller must retry with a fresh snapshot revision or new request id.
No locks, threads or interior mutability; all mutable state is private and mutated only by &mut apply. Snapshots are owned clones, so concurrent readers observe a consistent immutable copy.
Depends only on serde and serde_json for typed decoding plus std collections; SCHEMA cafe.control.v1 and Command op tags form the closed wire contract consumed by pairing and control layers.

FramePool is the bounded recorder-owned copy pool that copies borrowed row-pitch source bytes into preallocated tightly packed BGRA slots leased as OwnedFrame values, with no production defaults and no heap allocation on the hot path.

FramePool::new takes caller-supplied PoolLimits with all fields positive else ZeroLimits; it checked-multiplies slots by max_frame_bytes, reserves the global live-byte budget, then allocates exactly slots buffers of max_frame_bytes zeros.

copy_from takes a borrowed data slice plus width, height, source_stride and source_time describing caller memory never retained; it validates geometry, stride and length, pops a free slot, copies width*4 bytes per row skipping padding, returns OwnedFrame.

Admission order: InvalidGeometry for zero or over-limit width and height; ArithmeticOverflow on width*4 and width*height*4; FrameTooLarge when total exceeds max_frame_bytes; InvalidStride when source_stride is smaller; SourceTooShort when slice is short; Exhausted when no slot free.

Every error refuses without handing out a partial lease and without consuming a slot. Exhausted fails closed under load; callers must drop a leased frame or enlarge limits, never expect heap fallback.

User sees recording stall or frames dropped after a few frames with an empty or short file: pool exhausted because consumers hold OwnedFrames, frame larger than max_frame_bytes, or source stride and slice mismatch from a changed capture size.

Slots cycle free to leased to free: copy_from pops a buffer, OwnedFrame owns it, Drop swaps it out and pushes it back if free length is below slots. available, in_use and capacity expose free, slots-free and slots counts.

OwnedFrame always holds tightly packed width*height*4 BGRA bytes; pixels() returns exactly len bytes, packed_stride is width*4, while source_stride and source_time preserve the original row pitch and timestamp for diagnostics.

All live pool bytes are bounded by a process-global 2 GiB counter via FrameReservation CAS loop: ZeroLimits on zero, ArithmeticOverflow on checked_add overflow, FrameTooLarge when the limit would be exceeded. Reservation lives in the FramePool Arc.

Free list is guarded by a Mutex with poison recovery; global reservation uses atomic compare-exchange so simultaneous reservations cannot overbook. OwnedFrame is not Clone; Drop returns the buffer even if the pool handle was dropped.

Bytes flow from caller BorrowedFrame slice through per-row copy into a recycled Vec<u8> slot, out as OwnedFrame.pixels to the pipe writer; the buffer returns to the pool on drop, preserving reserved capacity across leases.
Depends only on std Mutex and atomics plus capsule_registry Clock timestamps; no allocator or OS handle beyond try_reserve_exact, which maps allocation failure to FrameTooLarge.
max_frame_bytes is an independent upper bound and may be smaller than max_width*max_height*4; configuring them inconsistently makes valid-geometry frames fail as FrameTooLarge at copy time.

CaptureHealth is the admission gate after an owned frame copy: it tracks one window generation and size plus border capability and decides whether each timestamped frame may enter the recorder or the source needs restart.

new takes HealthPolicy with nonzero stall_budget, nonzero width and height, and BorderStatus; Required or Available starts in Waiting, other border states start in BorderUnavailable. Zero budget or geometry returns InvalidPolicy or InvalidGeometry.

event feeds lifecycle signals Minimized, Restored, Waiting, Backpressure, SourceFailed, Closed, DeviceLost, Resized and BorderUnavailable; Closed, DeviceLost, ResizeRequired and GenerationMismatch are sticky and ignore later events until restart.

admit_frame takes generation, width, height, source_time and observed_at on one monotonic Clock domain; it enforces restart-terminal, generation, geometry, border/minimized, observation-clock, frozen-source and staleness checks in that order.

States: Waiting, Healthy, Minimized, Frozen, Closed, DeviceLost, ResizeRequired, GenerationMismatch, Backpressure, BorderUnavailable, SourceFailed, ClockRegression. Native failures dominate capability and temporary events; only explicit Restored clears Minimized.

Terminal states return Terminal; wrong generation sets GenerationMismatch; size change sets ResizeRequired; minimized or missing border returns NotAdmissible; observation clock going backward sets ClockRegression.

Non-increasing source_time sets Frozen and returns Frozen; source more than 1_000_000 ticks ahead of observed_at or older than stall_budget sets Frozen and returns StaleSource. Success records source and arrival and sets Healthy.

status(now) is the stall watchdog: it rejects backward now as ClockRegression, then if Healthy checks source within lead bound and both source-age and arrival-age inside stall_budget, else transitions to Frozen and returns current state.

User sees a paused, black or never-starting capture: minimized window, unavailable border, frozen duplicate timestamps, stale source beyond budget, or a resize that forces restart before recording can continue.
